observed_pattern.interpretation: Near-perfect precision with ~0.8-2.7% recall is incompatible with a mild 256-grid resolution deficit and indicates raster apparatus under-coverage.

root_cause.defect: The hard occupancy mask was derived from the same blurred PyTorch3D fragment list used for the soft gradient surrogate (blur_radius>0, faces_per_pixel=8). On a ~730k triangle projection, nearby non-covering front faces can consume the top-K fragment slots and exclude the actual covering triangle. Therefore 'hard = any(valid & dists<=0)' was not an exact hard union-of-triangles raster.
root_cause.consequence: Proxy parity measured fragment-list truncation, not the training mesh footprint.

hard_forward_raster.explanation: With zero blur only genuinely covering faces enter the rasterizer; one nearest covering face is sufficient for silhouette union coverage.

soft_backward_raster.explanation: Soft distance gradients are restricted to faces that actually support the current hard predicted boundary, preventing internal triangle edges from acting as silhouette loss.

stage13_semantic_parity.requirement: PyTorch3D zero-blur hard mask must byte/IoU-parity an exact Stage13 half-integer top-left raster of the same sampled training triangles in every view before optimizer start.
